chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Mufaddal ibn Salih, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:

Jibraeel descended upon Adam (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Adam! I have been commanded to give you a choice of one from three, so choose it and leave the other two.' Adam said to him: 'O Jibraeel! And what are the three?'

He said: 'The intellect, modesty, and religion.' Adam said: 'I have chosen the intellect.' So Jibraeel said to modesty and religion: 'Depart and leave him.' But they said: 'O Jibraeel! We have been commanded to remain with the intellect wherever it may be.' He said: 'Then that is your affair,' and he ascended.

key_terms.الدِّين: Din — Religion; the complete way of life including belief, worship, and moral conduct
key_terms.الْحَيَاء: Haya' — Modesty, bashfulness, shame; an ethical virtue that guides behavior
key_terms.الْعَقْل: 'Aql — Intellect; the faculty of reason and discernment, regarded as the highest gift to humanity in Shia theological thought

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali narrate that modesty and religion always accompany the intellect?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) narrates a cosmological account in which the angel Jibraeel was sent to Adam with a divine choice between three gifts: intellect ('aql), modesty (haya'), and religion (din). When Adam chose the intellect, modesty and religion refused to depart, declaring they were divinely commanded to accompany the intellect wherever it resided. This narrative presents intellect as the foundational human faculty upon which both moral virtue (modesty) and religious practice (din) are necessarily dependent — a key premise of the Book of 'Aql in al-Kafi.
